newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico May CPI rises 0.91 pct - Banco de Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Mexico May CPI rises 0.91 pct - Banco de Mexico.

text.p: Mexico's consumer price index rose 0.91 percent in May from the month before after rising 1.08 percent in April, Banco de Mexico said on Monday.
The central bank added that the producer price index rose 0.69 percent in May from the month before, compared to rise of 0.70 percent in April.
Banco de Mexico said it was the smallest monthly rise in the CPI since December 1994, the same month that the peso was drastically and suddenly devalued.
The central bank said that compared with the same month a year earlier the CPI was 21.23 percent higher, compared with 33.83 percent in the previous 12-month period.
The accumulated inflation rate for the first five months of the year was 7.71 percent, compared with 13.46 percent in the same period a year earlier.

It said that the main causes of inflation this year was an increase in prices of housing rents, local telephone service, household gas, gasoline, restaurantes, automobiles, soaps and detergents, soft drinks, poultry and beef, chiles, cucumbers, onions, oranges and coffee, among other items.
It said that the basic basket of consumer goods rose 0.79 percent in May from the month before.

A survey of 10 Mexican brokerages and research companies found expectations of a rise of 0.92 percent for May's CPI. Banacci brokerage and the CEESP think tank predicted exactly the actual increase of 0.91 percent.

In May, the producer price index of 0.69 percent was less than half the 1.46 percent registered in May 1996.
The PPI was 17.43 percent higher than in May 1996.
The accumulated increase for the first five months, excluding petroleum, was 6.22 percent compared to 12.86 percent in the first five months of 1996.
